title: Muhammad Suraj Salihu
text:
Welcome
This website is my bioinformatics portfolio and learning journal.
I am documenting the projects I build, the tools I learn, the problems I encounter and the progress I make along the way.
Rather than allowing a course to end when the lectures finish, I want to continue putting what I learn into practice.

title: Muhammad Suraj Salihu
text:
What I’m Learning


🧬 Bioinformatics
Sequence analysis, biological databases, conservation analysis and computational biology workflows.


Python
Python programming for data analysis, automation and bioinformatics.


Linux & Bash
Command-line tools, shell scripting and reproducible workflows.


📊 Data Analysis
Working with biological datasets, visualization and exploratory analysis.


Git & GitHub
Version control, project organization and collaborative development.


📖 Quarto
Creating reproducible reports, documentation and computational websites.

title: Muhammad Suraj Salihu
text:
Featured Project.

FLT3-Conserve
A bioinformatics project to explore sequence conservation across species using Python and biological sequence analysis, with a focus on the FLT3 gene. This is a project-based learning journey, but I exlore my research interest through it.
Status: In progress

title: About Me
text:
Muhammad Suraj Salihu


I am a final year medical student developing an interest in bioinformatics, computational biology and data-driven approaches to medicine.
My background in medicine and love for computers right before med school took over has made me interested in questions that sit at the intersection of biology, disease and computation.


First my fascination by just how much a computer can do plus my love for medicine.
My current focus is on building a strong foundation in:

Python
Linux
Bash scripting
Sequence analysis
Data visualization




I am still very early in this journey, so this website is intentionally also a record of my learning process.
I want to document not only successful projects, but also the problems I encounter and how I solve them. And the ones that straight up defeated me, of course

Last updated: August 2026

title: Learning Journey
text:
This page documents my progression through bioinformatics, programming and computational science.



I am developing practical skills in:

Biological sequence analysis
FASTA files
Biopython
Sequence alignment
Conservation analysis
Biological databases
Data visualization
Reproducible workflows





I am learning to use Python for:

Data manipulation
Automation
Biological sequence analysis

My current goal is to become comfortable enough with Python that I can solve biological problems rather than simply follow tutorials.




I am learning to work comfortably from the command line.
Topics include:

File and directory management
Pipes and redirection
ls
cd
cat
mkdir
Bash scripting (much faster than writing the same commands over and over again)
Fetching and processing data from databases via the command line





I am using GitHub to:

Track my work
Practice version control
Document projects
Maintain reproducible workflows
Build a public portfolio





I am using the challenge to strengthen my Python fundamentals.
Each completed exercise will be pushed to GitHub as I progress.




Learn → Build → make mistakes → Document → Share → Improve
